Luke 23:50–24:7; John 19:38–20:9."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"The subterranean realm of the dead—Sheol or Hades—with the phrase referring specifically to Christ’s descent to the dead rather than merely his entombment.","basis":["Acts 2:27,31, applying Psalm 16 to Christ’s not being abandoned to Hades.","Ephesians 4:9, especially when “the lower parts of the earth” is read as the underworld.","Romans 10:7, which associates bringing Christ up with descent into the abyss.","1 Peter 3:18–20 and 4:6, traditionally connected with Christ’s proclamation to the dead."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The literal interior or center of the physical earth, often identified with a spatially located underworld or hell.","basis":["A strongly spatial reading of “heart of the earth” in Matthew 12:40.","Traditional cosmological readings of passages mentioning Sheol, Hades, the abyss, or “lower parts of the earth,” such as Ephesians 4:9."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Jerusalem, the land of Israel, or the midst of the earthly human order, so that Jesus’ time under human custody or condemnation—not only his time in the tomb—fulfills the saying.","basis":["Use of “earth” or “land” as a possible rendering of Greek gē.","Attempts to reconcile Matthew 12:40’s “three days and three nights” with alternative passion chronologies."],"prominence":"rare"},{"meaning":"A general metaphor for profound humiliation, suffering, or apparent abandonment to death, without specifying either a tomb or an underworld location.","basis":["The death-and-deliverance pattern of Jonah 1–2.","Biblical poetic language associating deep places with death and distress, including Jonah 2:2–6 and Psalm 88:3–6."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad Christian consensus that the phrase refers to Jesus’ death and burial before resurrection. There is no equally settled consensus about the precise location implied: many interpret it simply as the grave, while significant traditional interpretation understands it as Hades or the realm of the dead."}
